memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When I came to the spring today, I said, "LORD, God of my master Abraham, if you will, please grant success to the journey on which I have come. See, I am standing beside this spring. If a young woman comes out to draw water and I say to her, 'Please let me drink a little water from your jar,' and if she says to me, 'Drink, and I'll draw water for your camels too,' let her be the one the LORD has chosen for my master's son." Before I finished praying in my heart, Rebekah came out, with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water, and I said to her, "Please give me a drink." She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, "Drink, and I'll water your camels too." So I drank, and she watered the camels also. I asked her, "Whose daughter are you?" She said, "The daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milkah bore to him." Then I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms, and I bowed down and worshiped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right road to get the granddaughter of my master's brother for his son. Now if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so I may know which way to turn.'" - Gen 24:42-49 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The servant retells everything that happened — his prayer at the well, God's swift answer, and how Rebekah did exactly as he had asked. And through it all, one name keeps returning: the Lord. "The LORD has chosen"; "the LORD... led me on the right road." He is careful to give God every ounce of the credit.

This is testimony at its best. The servant is not showing off his own skill or luck; he is telling the family what God has done. His whole account is designed to help them see God's hand so clearly that they cannot miss it.

We too are called to tell others what God has done. Sharing our story — how God answered, provided, or led — can build faith in listeners the way this servant's story moved Rebekah's family. You do not need clever arguments; you simply need to tell honestly what God has done in your life (Mark 5:19).

Notice also his humility at the end: "so I may know which way to turn." He has done his part and now leaves the outcome with God and with them. Testify to God's goodness, then trust Him with the response.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How often do I tell others what God has done for me?
2. Does my "story" give God the credit or myself?
3. Can I share honestly and leave the response to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to tell others honestly what You have done in my life, giving You all the glory. Make my testimony a blessing that draws others to trust You. Amen.
